analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction that an unaffordable £15,000 loan was granted and alleges financial loss and material distress (CH-1).
analysis.summary: Customer says a £15,000 personal loan was lent in March when they were on a zero hours contract with two maxed-out credit cards. They now pay £410 a month and cannot cover it. They report not sleeping and being 'at the end of my rope'. Acknowledgement was sent on 2026-09-23 and a holding reply on 2026-10-14. Final response is due 2026-11-17 (At risk). There is a possible vulnerability needing referral and an affordability complaint for Lending Specialists. No evidence is listed.

timeline.event: Customer says £15,000 loan was granted while on a zero hours contract with two credit cards maxed out.
Customer emailed asking for an update; holding reply sent.

analysis.severity_reason: Vulnerable customer at risk of harm (CH-6): financial difficulty, sleeplessness and distress. Customer cannot afford £410 a month on a £15,000 loan. Actual financial loss is not quantified.

vulnerability.suggested_support: Ask the customer sensitively about support needs and offer reasonable adjustments, such as a named contact and preferred contact method. Refer to Vulnerable Customer Support and consider forbearance options through Lending Specialists.

analysis.routing_reason: The complaint alleges an unaffordable lending decision, so Lending Specialists must handle it (ESC-1, LND-1). The customer shows financial difficulty plus signs of wellbeing risk, which triggers a VUL-4 referral to Vulnerable Customer Support.

policy_citations.quote: where the customer alleges they have suffered (or may suffer) financial loss, material distress or material inconvenience
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The customer alleges distress and difficulty paying, so this is a complaint.

policy_citations.quote: Complaints that a lending decision was unaffordable or irresponsible must be handed to Lending Specialists.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The customer says the loan should not have been granted given their income and debts.

policy_citations.quote: Cases with a vulnerability indicator *and* any of: financial difficulty, risk to health or wellbeing, suspected financial abuse, or bereavement must be referred to the Vulnerable Customer Support team.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Financial difficulty and sleeplessness or distress are both present.

policy_citations.quote: a vulnerable customer at risk of harm
If in doubt, record it as a possible vulnerability and ask the customer, sensitively, whether they need any support.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Indirect statements indicate possible vulnerability and the customer has not been asked.

handover.complaint_summary: Customer says a £15,000 loan was granted in March despite a zero hours contract and two maxed-out credit cards. They now cannot afford the £410 monthly payment and report distress and poor sleep.
handover.products_and_accounts: Personal loan, account [ACCOUNT_NUMBER_1]. Credit cards mentioned but no references given.
handover.desired_outcome: Not explicitly stated. Customer says 'I don't think you should have given me that loan.'
actions_taken: Holding reply sent after customer chased (2026-10-14)
handover.vulnerability_assessment: Indicators found: resilience (cannot afford repayments, maxed-out cards, zero hours income) and possible health (cannot sleep, 'at the end of my rope'). Customer has not been asked about support needs.

analysis.suggested_next_step: Hand over to Lending Specialists, with a VUL-4 referral to Vulnerable Customer Support, today. Because of the At risk deadline, arrange weekly team leader review (CH-5) and contact the customer sensitively to ask about support needs.
